title: Concrete Short Cap 1-2 Pole
description: Concrete Poles with a 1-2 Alternating Sidearm configuration and a short cap which lies directly on top of the pole are most commonly found in Eastern Cordoba

title: Wooden Even Insulators Config Pole
description: Wooden Poles with 2 or 3 insulators and the central insulator (if the pole has one) perfectly in the center of the two insulators on the edges of the crossbar are found throughout the whole country with the notable exceptions of Mendoza and San Luis and are exceptionally rare in Santa Fe, San Juan, La Rioja, Cordoba and La Pampa - especially in comparison to the surrounding states in the plains region of Buenos Aires, Entre Rios, Santiago del Estero and Chaco in which this pole type is common.

title: Concrete No Cap 1-2 Pole
description: This pole is by far most commonly found in Buenos Aires, however there exist some more rare exceptions in other states, use this as a confirmation for your regionguess in combination with other clues or as a baseline if there are no other clues

title: Concrete Short Top No Cap 1-2 Pole
description: This pole is common in most of the plains region, however quite rare in the states of Cordoba and Buenos Aires.

title: Concrete Standard Top No Cap 1-2 Pole
description: This pole type can be recognized by the top extension being around the same length as the section between the two sidearms. It is the standard pole configuration in Santiago del Estero with around 80% of all similar concrete poles being of this exact type. More rarely it can also be found in Santa Fe and Entre Rios.
